subject: economics
topicDisplay: International Trade And The Global Economy
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Comparative advantage is based on which country has the:
options: Lower opportunity cost of producing a good
questions.explain: Comparative advantage means a country can produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another.

questions.q: A criticism of multinational companies operating in developing countries is that they may:
options: Exploit cheap labour and send profits back to their home country
Refuse to employ any local workers
questions.explain: TNCs are criticised for using low-wage labour and repatriating profits rather than reinvesting locally.

questions.q: An export subsidy paid to domestic firms is intended to:
options: Increase the price of imports directly
Make their goods cheaper and more competitive abroad
questions.explain: An export subsidy lowers domestic firms' costs so their goods are cheaper and more competitive overseas.

questions.q: Free trade means:
options: International trade without barriers such as tariffs and quotas
Trade with high tariffs on all goods
questions.explain: Free trade is trade between countries unrestricted by tariffs, quotas or other barriers.

questions.q: A current account SURPLUS means the value of a country's:
questions.explain: A current account surplus occurs when the value of exports exceeds the value of imports.

questions.q: A current account deficit on the balance of payments means a country is:
options: Importing more goods and services than it exports
questions.explain: A current account deficit occurs when the value of imports exceeds the value of exports.

questions.q: Falling transport and communication costs have encouraged globalisation by:
options: Raising the cost of moving goods
Making international trade and investment easier and cheaper
questions.explain: Cheaper transport and communications have lowered the cost of trading and investing across borders.

questions.q: A tariff is best described as:
options: A limit on the quantity of imports
questions.explain: A tariff is a tax placed on imports to make them dearer and protect domestic producers.

questions.q: Which is recorded as a CREDIT (money flowing in) on the current account?
options: The value of goods a country exports
Money spent by UK tourists abroad
Profits sent overseas by foreign firms
questions.explain: Exports earn money from abroad and are recorded as credits on the current account.

questions.q: A developed economy, compared with a developing economy, typically has:
options: A larger share of subsistence farming
A higher GDP per person and standard of living
questions.explain: Developed economies generally have higher GDP per head and living standards than developing ones.

questions.q: A trading bloc, such as the EU single market, is a group of countries that:
options: Reduce trade barriers between member countries
questions.explain: A trading bloc lowers or removes trade barriers between its members to encourage trade.

questions.q: A consumer benefit of free trade is usually:
options: Lower prices and a wider choice of goods
questions.explain: Free trade increases competition and access to foreign goods, lowering prices and widening choice.

questions.q: If a currency APPRECIATES (rises in value), imports become:
questions.explain: A stronger currency makes imports cheaper and exports more expensive abroad.

questions.q: A quota is a form of protectionism that:
options: Sets a physical limit on the quantity of a good that can be imported
questions.explain: A quota limits the quantity of imports allowed, restricting foreign competition.

questions.q: Globalisation refers to:
options: The increasing integration and interconnection of the world's economies
Countries trading less with each other
The creation of a single world government
questions.explain: Globalisation is the growing interdependence and integration of economies through trade and investment.

questions.q: One benefit a multinational company can bring to a host (developing) country is:
options: Creating jobs and bringing investment and technology
Always lowering local wages to zero
questions.explain: TNCs can create employment and bring investment, skills and technology to host countries.

questions.q: A country gains from international trade mainly because it can:
options: Print more of its own currency
Specialise in goods it produces relatively efficiently and trade for the rest
questions.explain: Trade lets countries specialise where they are most efficient and import other goods more cheaply.

questions.q: Absolute advantage exists when a country can produce a good:
options: Using more workers than any rival
Using fewer resources (more efficiently) than another country
At a higher money price than its rivals
questions.explain: A country has absolute advantage when it can produce a good using fewer resources than another country.

questions.q: An argument FOR protectionism is to:
questions.explain: Protectionism can shield young domestic industries until they grow strong enough to compete.

questions.q: If a country's currency DEPRECIATES (falls in value), its exports become:
questions.explain: A weaker currency makes exports cheaper to foreign buyers and imports dearer at home.

questions.q: If the pound depreciates, the most likely effect on a UK firm importing parts is:
questions.explain: A weaker pound makes foreign goods and parts more expensive, raising importers' costs.

questions.q: Imposing a tariff on imported steel is most likely to:
options: Raise the price of imported steel and protect domestic steel firms
Reduce the price of all goods
Lower the price of imported steel
questions.explain: A tariff raises import prices, making domestic producers more competitive against foreign rivals.
